key_insight: Detonation-sprayed hydroxyapatite coatings on Grade 2 titanium can substantially improve tribological performance, with the best results at intermediate O2/C2H2 ratios of 3.0–3.3.
engineering_relevance: The study points to a practical route for making titanium implants more wear-resistant and biocompatible for physiological service conditions.
method: Hydroxyapatite was detonation-sprayed onto commercially pure Grade 2 titanium.
O2/C2H2 ratio was varied from 2.6 to 3.7 to tune coating formation.
Coatings were evaluated by XRD, surface characterization, and dry/Ringer’s-solution tribological tests.
evidence_signal: XRD showed dominant hydroxyapatite with some alpha-tricalcium phosphate, and tribology tests found the lowest wear and best friction behavior at O2/C2H2 ratios of 3.0 and 3.3.
watch_item: The coatings are structurally heterogeneous and performance depends strongly on process window control, so scale-up will require tight spray parameter optimization and adhesion verification.
paper_title: STUDY OF TRIBOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF BIOCOATINGS BY DETONATION SPRAYING METHOD
